messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Advanced QGIS Spatial Analysis for Genetics
messages.subject_clean: Advanced QGIS Spatial Analysis for Genetics
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

A reminder - Connect genetic data to the geographic context shaping sampled populations. Advanced QGIS: Spatial Analysis 2.0 is a 2-day seminar livestreaming August 11?12 with Nick Bearman (University College London and Geospatial Training Solutions). Spatial overlays, point-in-polygon operations, and coordinate-based data integration support rigorous analysis of geographic genetic patterns. Learn to join diverse datasets, conduct access analyses, and aggregate spatial results into meaningful metrics. Apply QGIS methods to relate sampling locations and spatial context to genetic research questions.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/advanced-qgis-spatial-analysis-20
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Online course. Invasion Genomics in R. 12-14-16 October
messages.subject_clean: Online course. Invasion Genomics in R. 12-14-16 October
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Registrations are open for our online course ?Invasion Genomics in R?, taking place 12, 14 & 16 October.
 
Course website: [ https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/invasion-genomics/ ]( https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/invasion-genomics/ ) 
 
Designed to foster international participation, the course combines recorded lectures, self-paced practical tutorials with annotated R scripts, and live remote instructor support. Participants can progress through the materials at their own pace while having the opportunity to ask questions and discuss challenges with the instructor. The format is particularly suited to participants across different time zones.
 
The course provides a practical introduction to invasion genomics, focusing on three key themes:
Movement dynamics ? investigating invasion sources, dispersal pathways, genetic diversity, and population structure
Adaptation dynamics ? applying selection outlier detection methods to investigate adaptive processes
Environmental adaptation ? using genotype-by-environment association (GEA) methods to explore how environmental conditions shape adaptive outcomes
The course is aimed at graduate students, researchers, and professionals interested in applying genomic approaches to invasion biology. 

Includes: Recorded lectures, guided practicals, annotated R scripts, and live remote support
Participants will gain both fundamental knowledge and practical experience to help them apply invasion genomic approaches in their own research.
 
For the full list of our courses and workshops, please visit: [ https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/ ]( https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/ )
 
 
 
Best regards,
 
Carlo

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Genomics for Ecological and Evolutionary Studies
messages.subject_clean: Genomics for Ecological and Evolutionary Studies
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

Develop practical genomic data skills for ecological and evolutionary research questions. Genomics for Ecological and Evolutionary Studies led by Giulio Formenti (Vertebrate Genome Lab, The Rockefeller University) and Guido Gallo (Department of Biosciences, University of Milan) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Sequencing-data analysis and bioinformatics workflows can help genetics researchers connect genomic evidence to ecological and evolutionary questions. Participants practise obtaining public data, aligning short and long reads, calling variants, inspecting variant files, and comparing alignments with command-line tools. These methods can be applied alongside R-based genetic-data analysis to evaluate sequencing technologies, manage genomic datasets, and investigate biodiversity and evolutionary history.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/genomics-for-ecological-and-evolutionary-1
Further information is available on the Instats course page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Appraising quantitative research in genetics
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

Genetic analyses are easier to assess when claims, designs, and evidence remain aligned. Appraising and Improving Quantitative Research led by Centre for Applied Statistics Courses (CASC) (University College London) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Critical appraisal of study design, bias, model assumptions, and sensitivity analyses can strengthen genetic data-analysis decisions. Learn to align research questions, estimands, sampling, and analytical choices while evaluating reported uncertainty and causal claims. Apply reproducibility checks, reporting frameworks, and transparent workflows when reviewing or improving quantitative genetics research in R.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/appraising-and-improving-quantitative-re-1
The course page includes the curriculum and enrollment details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-genetics] Spatial data and R for genetics
messages.subject_clean: Spatial data and R for genetics
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-GENETICS members

A reminder - Bring geographic context into genetic data analysis and presentation. Introduction to Spatial Data and R as a GIS 2.0 is a 2-day seminar livestreaming August 18?19 with Nick Bearman (University College London and Geospatial Training Solutions). Import, process, and visualise spatial data in R with sf, choropleth mapping, and map customisation. Automate repeated map production and work across spatial data formats, coordinate reference systems, and point data. Genetic researchers can use these methods to examine and present geographic structure alongside genetic datasets.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/introduction-to-spatial-data-and-r-as-a-4
Please circulate this reminder if it is relevant to colleagues or students.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
